rows.observation: Global diesel shortage expected to persist until mid-2027 (IEA warning)
research: "finding": "The IEA’s October 2026 Oil Market Report warns that global diesel (middle‑distillate) markets will remain tight well into 2027, with inventories unlikely to rebuild before the second half of 2027.",

"importance": "Major diesel‑importing regions (Europe, Africa, Latin America, parts of Asia) and sectors that depend on diesel for transport, agriculture, heating and power generation are affected; persistent tightness drives wholesale and retail diesel prices to record highs, feeds inflation, raises costs of goods and services, and strains energy‑security frameworks.",

"evidence": "Diesel markets remained under significant strain as prolonged supply disruptions forced counter‑seasonal stock draws ahead of autumn refinery maintenance and peak winter demand. Gasoil supply falls short of meeting demand in 4Q26, suggesting that the replenishment of lost inventories, outside of typical seasonal fluctuations, is unlikely before the second half of 2027. Combined losses of diesel exports from the Middle East and Russia totalled 1.3 million barrels per day in September. Wholesale diesel prices exceeded $200/barrel in Singapore and reached all‑time highs of around $220/barrel in Europe and the United States.",
"sources": [
"International Energy Agency – Oil Market Report – October 2026",
"Reuters, “Tight diesel supplies could persist well into next year as conflicts curb output from the Middle East and Russia,” 14 Oct 2026",
"The National, “Diesel shortage to persist into 2027 as Iran war disrupts supply, IEA warns”",
"CoinPaper, “IEA warns diesel shortages could keep global inflation high”",
"lufkindailynews.com, “Global diesel shortages could persist well into 2027, warns the IEA”"

"context": "Geopolitical: ongoing war in the Middle East (including Iran‑related tensions) and Russia’s sanctions‑driven export restrictions; Ukraine’s drone strikes on Russian refineries have further reduced diesel supply. Market dynamics: diesel (middle distillate) is a price‑inelastic fuel critical for transport, agriculture, and heating; demand has held up despite higher prices, partly due to government consumer‑relief programmes. Inventory situation: global observed oil inventories were ~509 million barrels below pre‑war levels at end‑September 2026, with diesel comprising a large share of those strategic reserves, leaving markets more vulnerable to further shocks. Outlook: the IEA forecasts global oil demand to fall by 2.6 million bpd in 2026, with diesel accounting for ~25 % of that decline; supply is expected to recover modestly in 2027, but the diesel‑gasoil balance will remain tight in the first half and only ease in the second half.",

"uncertainty": "The timeline depends on the resolution of Middle‑East and Russia export disruptions; renewed attacks could prolong the shortage while a diplomatic breakthrough could accelerate inventory rebuild. Potential geopolitical shocks (e.g., hurricane impacts on Gulf Coast refining) or extreme‑weather events could further disrupt supply and push the timeline beyond mid‑2027. Policy actions such as releases of strategic reserves or eased import restrictions may modestly affect prices but are unlikely to fully offset the accumulated deficit.",
